Author: K.Lakshman
Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Writ Petition No.8690 of 2023
Order:

(Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice K.Lakshman) Heard Sri. P.Vishnu Vardhan Reddy, learned counsel representing Sri. N. Vishal, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Mujeeb Kumar sadasivuni,
learned special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General.
2.

This writ petition is filed for challenging the detention order in No. 06/PD CELL/
CCRB/RCKD/2023, dated 09.02.2023 by 2nd respondent and as confirmed by the 1st respondent vide GO RT No.443 dated 23.03.2023, petitioner mother of the detenue filed the present writ petition.
3. Perusal of the record would reveal that five cases were registered against the detenue.

On the complaint lodged by Ms. Mucharla Vaishali (victim girl) Police Adibatla Police Station registered a case in Crime No.367 of 2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 419,354(D), 506 r/w 109 IPC and 66 C-IT Act 2000.

Since the punishment for the offences alleged against the detenue is seven years and below seven years, the investigating officer has invoked the procedure laid down under Section 41 A of Crpc and served notice under Section 41 A of Crpc on 17.09.2022.

The allegations against the detenue are that he has created a fake ID in the name of the victim girl in instagram app, went to her college, constructed a flakes room in front of her house with a view to create nuisance and threaten her and her family members.

4. Crime No.486 of 2022 was registered against the detenue on the complaint lodged by father of the victim i.e., Ms. Mucherla Vaishali pending by the Police, Adibatla Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 147,148,307,324,363,427,506,354,452,380 r/w 149 IPC.

The allegation in the said complaint was that the detenue, he along with 50 associates came to his house vehicles with arms etc trespass into his house, kidnapped his daughter i.e., victim (Ms. Mucherla Vaishali) and attempted to murder.

5. Crime No.493 of 2022 was registered against the detenue by Police, Adibatla Police Station on the complaint lodged by the supervisor of Veda Convention Centre which is opposite to the house of the victim for the offences punishable under Sections 148,452,324,427,506,504 r/w 149 of IPC.

The Kodudula Narayanamma vs The State Of Telangana, on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76604432/
1 detenue was released on bail on 03.02.2023.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Allegations against the detenue are that, he along with 30 to 35 associate came to victim girl's house, in the quarrel, they have damaged the gate etc., of the function hall.

6. Crime No. 501 of 2022 was registered against the detenue by the very same Police, Adibatla Police Station on the complaint lodged by the victim girl for the offences punishable under sections 417,420 IPC on allegation that the detenue cheated her, by using her friendship for a period of few days, blamed her and her parents.

7. 5th Crime No.504 of 2022 was registered by Police, Adibatla Police Station on the complaint lodged by the victim girl against the detenue for the offences punishable under Section 354-C, 509 r/w 34 of IPC.
The allegation against the detenue is that he has released the photographs of the victim to the media.

8. Relying on the said crimes, 2nd respondent has invoked the procedure laid down in The Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-Leggers Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas,
Immoral Traffic Offenders Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders,
Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986.

entities.text: Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-Leggers Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Herein, after referred as Act 1986 on 09.02.2023 on the ground that the acts of the detenue disturbed the public order, and to prevent him from committing further similar offences.
9. Sri. P. Vishnu Vardan Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that there is no disturbance to the public order and it is only of law and order problem.
Even though the respondent No.2 has invoked the Act 1986 and issued detention order and there is no disturbance to the public order.
It is matrimonial dispute between the petitioner and the victim.
They fell in love and they went to Goa on their own and married on 04.08.2021 in a temple.
The detenue has filed O.P.No.1364 of 2022 under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act against victim girl for restoration of Conjugal Rights.
The facts of the present case are not falling within the definition of Section 2(g) of the Act,1986.
He has placed reliance on the principle laid down by Apex Court and this Court.
10. Even then, the respondent No.2 invoked the provisions of the Act, 1986 and passed impugned detention order.

The respondent No.1 approved the said detention order by way of issuing G.o.Rt.No.443 dated 23.03.2023, and both are in violation of the provisions, procedure laid down under the Act and contrary to the principle laid down in Apex Court.
With the said submissions, he sought to set aside the said proceedings.

11. Whereas, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that though it is a matrimonial dispute, there are serious allegations against the detenue.
He came to the victim girl house along with the 50 people and created a panic situation which disturbed the public order, more particularly disturbances to the women/girls of the locality.
Even one solitary case is enough to invoke procedure laid down in the 1986 Act.

The allegations Kodudula Narayanamma vs The State Of Telangana, on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76604432/
2 levelled against the detenue are very serious and five cases were registered against him.

entities.text: Kodudula Narayanamma vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the nature of offence and manner in which it was committed by the detenue and other aspects the respondent No.2 rightly passed detention order and the 1st respondent rightly confirmed the said order.
With the said submissions, he sought to dismiss the present writ petition.
12. As discussed supra, five cases were registered against the detenue herein.
In all the aforesaid crimes, the allegations against the detenue are with regard to disputes between him and victim girl.

Perusal of the complaints in all the aforesaid crimes would reveal that the detenue and victim girl fell in love and according to detenue they went to Goa and he has paid about eight (8) lakhs to the victim girl by way of transfer to her account and in proof of the same, he has filed copy of the bank statement and paytm.
She has changed her mind at the instance of her father and implicated the detenue in all the aforesaid cases.
They married in a Temple.
In proof of that he has filed photographs.

Out of 5 crimes, 4 crimes were registered on the complaint lodged by victim girl and her father, one crime was registered on the complaint of supervisor of the Veda Convention Centre which is opposite to the house of the victim girl.
Issue is one and the same.
13. Perusal of record would reveal that detenue had filed O.P.No.1364 of 2022 under Section 9 of Hindu Marraige Act seeking restoration of Conjugal Rights.
The dispute between the detenue and victim girl is with regard to love affair and marraige performed by them.
According to us, there is no disturbance to public order, much less disturbance to the peace and tranquility in the society.
14. All the aforesaid cases were registered from 17.09.2022 to 15.12.2022 i.e., within a span of three months.
Dispute is one and the same.
The said dispute do not fall within the definition of the "habitual".
Without considering the said facts, the respondent No.2 has invoked the procedure laid down under the Act, 1986 by way of issuing detention order on 09.02.2023.

Without appreciating the aforesaid said facts, the respondent No.1 has confirmed the said detention order by way of issuing G.O.Rt.No.443 dated 23.03.2023.
15.

In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
"...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some?

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.
A District .

(1966) 1 SCR 709 Magistrate is entitled to take action Kodudula Narayanamma vs The State Of Telangana, on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76604432/
3 under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances.

entities.text: Kodudula Narayanamma vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.
It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."
Similar view was reiterated by the Apex Court in Arun Ghosh v. State of West Bengal2.

entities.text: Arun Ghosh v. State of West Bengal2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraphs are extracted below:
7. The question whether a man has only committed a breach of law and order or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the public order, according to the dictum laid down in the above case, is a question of degree and the extent of the reach of the act upon the society.
Public order is what the French call "order . (1970) 1 SCC 98 publique" and is something more than ordinary maintenance of law and order.

The test to be adopted in determining whether an act affects law and order or public order, as laid down in the above case, is: Does it lead to disturbance of the current of life of the community so as to amount to a disturbance of the public order or does it affect merely an individual leaving the tranquillity of the society undisturbed?
8.

The principle enunciated above has been followed by this Court in the case of Nagendra Nath Mondal v. State of West Bengal [(1972) 1 SCC 498] , and Nandlal Roy alias Honda Dulal Roy alias Pagea v. State of West Bengal (WP No. 15 of 1972, decided on April 11, 1972) [(1972) 2 SCC 524] .

entities.text: Nagendra Nath Mondal v. State of West Bengal [(1972) 1 SCC 498]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Nandlal Roy alias Honda Dulal Roy alias Pagea v. State of West Bengal (WP No. 15 of 1972
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of what has been observed above, we have no doubt that each one of the incidents of September 26, 1971 and November 4, 1971, was prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.

When two passengers are robbed at the point of knife while travelling in a third class compartment of a running train the act of the miscreants affects not only the passengers who are deprived of their valuables but also the other passengers who watch the whole thing in fear as helpless spectators.
There is bound to be consequent terror and panic amongst the travelling public.
Likewise, attack directed against a police party on the platform of a railway station by exploding bombs is bound to create panic and confusion among the passengers at the railway station.
The acts in question in the very nature of things would adversely affect the even tempo of life of the community and cause a general disturbance of public tranquillity.

16. Apex Court and Division Bench of this Court time and again held that preventive detention can be passed only in rarest of the rare cases to prevent the detenue from committing the similar offences.
Authorities have to consider the entire facts and maintain on record and shall follow the procedure laid down under the Act, 1986 scrupulously.

In the present case, there is consideration of Kodudula Narayanamma vs The State Of Telangana, on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76604432/
4 the said aspects.

entities.text: Kodudula Narayanamma vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that the respondent authorities have not taken steps by opposing bail applications and by way of filing the applications seeking to cancel the bail in the 1st crime on the ground that the detenue has committed similar offences when he was on bail in the earlier crime.
Without initiating such steps the respondent authorities cannot invoke the procedure laid down on the Act 1986 by issuing impugned detention order.
Viewed from any angle the impugned detention order, confirmed by respondent No.1 by G.O.Rt.No.443 dated 23.03.2023 are illegal and they are liable to be set aside.

17. Accordingly, this Writ Petition is allowed with a direction to respondent authorities to release the detenue i.e., Kandula Naveen Reddy S/o Koti Reddy forthwith if he is no longer not required in any other criminal case.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
